jurisdiction.venue: Regional Court of Würzburg, Germany (EPPO Munich)

headline: E.P.P.O. Indicts Three in Bavaria Over Alleged €48 Million ‘Second-Hand’ Smartphone VAT Scheme
deck: European prosecutors in Munich filed charges at the Regional Court of Würzburg accusing three electronics-trade executives of routing brand-new phones through E.U. and U.K. shell firms disguised as used goods to abuse margin taxation. All defendants are presumed innocent.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: EPPO Munich indicted three individuals at the Regional Court of Würzburg in Investigation Mela over an alleged €48 million ($52.2M) cross-border VAT scheme active since 2018 disguising new mobile phones as second-hand goods under margin taxation; defendants presumed innocent.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: If proven, the scheme would mirror slapping 'used' stickers on factory-sealed smartphones to dodge sales tax across an entire regional retail chain
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Aggravated tax-evasion indictment with pre-trial asset freezes and multi-year prison exposure if proven

sources.title: Investigation Mela: EPPO indicts three individuals in €48 million VAT fraud case involving electronic goods

interactive_art_spec.caption: The Regional Court of Würzburg (Landgericht Würzburg) in Bavaria, where the European Public Prosecutor’s Office filed an indictment against three individuals in Investigation Mela.
